title: Convolution as a linear operator; convolutional networks
summary: Cross-correlation as a shared linear map, adjoint gradients, shapes/receptive fields, shift counterexamples and detector verification.

objectives.description: Define convolution/cross-correlation and derive their linear operator and adjoint.
Calculate CNN shapes, parameters and receptive fields.
Prove equivariance under stated boundary rules and disprove blanket pooling invariance.
Gradient-check a local detector and design fair architecture/transfer comparisons.

preparation.description: Read convolution, padding/stride, pooling, parameter counts and transfer-learning overview. Check the limits of invariance claims.

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A convolution with bias is a linear map.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The kernel operation is linear; a nonzero bias makes the layer affine.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Pooling guarantees invariance to every image translation.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Window boundaries, stride and padding can change outputs under small shifts.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A transposed convolution is the inverse of convolution.
commonMisconceptions.correction: It is the adjoint of a stated linear map; information loss often prevents inversion.
